description: Hand-labelled search evaluation set for the RadLex concept lookup. Every expected RID was established by direct label/synonym lookup against the graph, never by running the ranker under test, so the labels stay independent of the thing they measure. A phrase may map to several acceptable RIDs; scoring is hit@1-in-set. An empty expected_rids with expect_miss true means a MISS is the correct answer, and returning a confident match instead is a failure. Absence claims must be verified with a normalized comparison, not a raw LIKE: a spaced query will not match a hyphenated label, which is exactly how the 'crazy paving' case was mislabelled as a gap.

cases.note: Report drops 'pulmonary'. Word-boundary matching misses this entirely.
Exact synonym of 'upper lobe of left lung'. Must stay exact after the change.
Regression guard: substring search ranked this 67th of 69, behind 'hepatocellular carcinoma'.

Legitimately maps to more than one concept: the margin descriptor and the nodule itself. BM25 ranks 'spiculated' (RID34284) first, which is arguably also acceptable but is not a report-level finding, so it is excluded.
Unhyphenated and plural against a hyphenated singular label.
Verified absent from labels and synonyms. A MISS is correct; the agent is expected to expand the abbreviation and retry. Stemming does not help here.
Control: must remain an exact match.
RadLex has no hilar-specific lymphadenopathy concept; 'lymphadenopathy' is the correct anchor. Verified no '%hilar lymph node%' label exists.
Descriptive phrasing for lymphadenopathy; no lexical overlap with the label.

cases.phrase: posterior segmental branch of the right lower lobe pulmonary artery
cases.note: Reads as absent but RadLex has it as 'right lower lobe posterior segment artery'. Concluding MISS here produces a duplicate proposal, the exact failure this work targets.
Tokenizer guard. With DuckDB's default ignore pattern digits are stripped and this returns 'cesium'. Requires ignore='(\.|[^a-z0-9])+'.
Category 4 must outrank 4B/4C. Indistinguishable without digits.

Two legitimate senses: RID29198 'first thoracic vertebra' is the anatomical structure and is preferred; RID6151 'T1' is the thoracic spine level descriptor. Both accepted. Note RID6151 is also how T1-weighted imaging would be phrased, so digit preservation alone does not disambiguate sense.
Guards the decision to keep DuckDB's english stopword list: 'of' is dropped at index and query time.
Exact label RID5598 is obsolete and outranks the live concept on BM25. Correct answer is the replacement 'vascular stent'; an obsolete top hit without replaced_by_rid is a failure.

RadLex has 'crazy-paving pattern' (RID43256) and 'crazy-paving sign' (RID35120). This case was originally mislabelled as a true gap because the verifying query used '%crazy paving%' with a space, which cannot match the hyphenated label -- the same hyphenation trap the search normalizer exists to handle. Kept as a regression against re-introducing it.
